page: Microsoft Azure D4ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 server family. It runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 236 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mix of average and weak capabilities, with notable strengths in single-threaded tasks. The single-threaded gzip compression performance is in the top tier at 36.47 GB/sec, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 15.05 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4653.8 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 29.54 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show average read-only performance, reaching 344.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 43.94 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while large block write bandwidth is weak at 23.77 GB/sec. Passmark testing yields average scores across CPU, memory, database operations, and encryption metrics.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ds_v7 offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated compute resources with local storage. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage reduces the immediate need for external storage attachments for temporary data. The hardware profile is suited for workloads that benefit from high single-core performance and vector instruction sets, such as lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and single-threaded data processing. It is less suited for highly parallelized, multi-threaded compute tasks due to its lower multi-core benchmark results.
